poems.title: Hope is the thing with feathers
poems.text:
Hope is the thing with feathers
That perches in the soul,
And sings the tune without the words,
And never stops at all.

poems.title: Song of Myself
poems.text:
I believe a leaf of grass is no less than the journey-work of the stars,
And the pismire is equally perfect, and a grain of sand,
And the tree-toad is a chef-d'oeuvre for the highest,
And the running blackberry would adorn the parlors of heaven.

poems.title: Stopping by Woods on a Snowy Evening
poems.text:
The woods are lovely, dark and deep,
But I have promises to keep,
And miles to go before I sleep,
And miles to go before I sleep.

poems.title: Nature
poems.text: To speak truly, few adult persons can see nature. Most persons do not see the sun. At least they have a very superficial seeing. The sun illuminates only the eye of the man, but shines into the eye and the heart of the child.

poems.title: Walden
poems.text: I went to the woods because I wished to live deliberately, to front only the essential facts of life, and see if I could not learn what it had to teach, and not, when I came to die, discover that I had not lived.

poems.title: Auguries of Innocence
poems.text:
To see a World in a Grain of Sand
And a Heaven in a Wild Flower,
Hold Infinity in the palm of your hand
And Eternity in an hour.

poems.title: The Old Pond
poems.text:
An old silent pond
A frog jumps into the pond—
Splash! Silence again.

poems.title: A Dream Within a Dream
poems.text:
All that we see or seem
Is but a dream within a dream.

poems.title: The World of Dew
poems.text:
The world of dew
is the world of dew.
And yet, and yet—

poems.title: A Psalm of Life
poems.text:
Tell me not, in mournful numbers,
Life is but an empty dream!
For the soul is dead that slumbers,
And things are not what they seem.

poems.title: Endymion
poems.text:
A thing of beauty is a joy for ever:
Its loveliness increases; it will never
Pass into nothingness.

poems.title: I Wandered Lonely as a Cloud
poems.text:
I wandered lonely as a cloud
That floats on high o'er vales and hills,
When all at once I saw a crowd,
A host, of golden daffodils.

poems.title: Ozymandias
poems.text:
Look on my Works, ye Mighty, and despair!
Nothing beside remains. Round the decay
Of that colossal Wreck, boundless and bare
The lone and level sands stretch far away.

poems.title: Spring Rain
poems.text:
Scampering over saucers—
the sound of a rat.
Cold, cold.

poems.title: I'm Nobody! Who are you?
poems.text:
I'm Nobody! Who are you?
Are you – Nobody – too?
Then there's a pair of us!
Don't tell! they'd advertise – you know!

poems.title: She Walks in Beauty
poems.text:
She walks in beauty, like the night
Of cloudless climes and starry skies;
And all that's best of dark and bright
Meet in her aspect and her eyes.

poems.title: O Captain! My Captain!
poems.text:
O Captain! my Captain! our fearful trip is done,
The ship has weather'd every rack, the prize we sought is won,
The port is near, the bells I hear, the people all exulting.

poems.title: There Will Come Soft Rains
poems.text:
There will come soft rains and the smell of the ground,
And swallows circling with their shimmering sound;
And frogs in the pools singing at night,
And wild plum trees in tremulous white.

poems.title: Ulysses
poems.text: To strive, to seek, to find, and not to yield.

poems.title: The Wound
poems.text: The wound is the place where the Light enters you.

poems.title: Remember
poems.text:
Better by far you should forget and smile
Than that you should remember and be sad.

poems.title: Patterns
poems.text:
I walk down the garden paths,
And all the daffodils
Are blowing, and the bright blue squills.
I walk down the patterned garden-paths
In my stiff, brocaded gown.

poems.title: To a Mouse
poems.text:
The best-laid schemes o' mice an' men
Gang aft agley,
An' lea'e us nought but grief an' pain,
For promis'd joy!

poems.title: The Ballad of Reading Gaol
poems.text:
Yet each man kills the thing he loves,
By each let this be heard,
Some do it with a bitter look,
Some with a flattering word.

poems.title: The Prophet
poems.text: Work is love made visible. And if you cannot work with love but only with distaste, it is better that you should leave your work and sit at the gate of the temple and take alms of those who work with joy.

poems.title: The Darkling Thrush
poems.text:
So little cause for carolings
Of such ecstatic sound
Was written on terrestrial things
Afar or nigh around.

poems.title: The Sun Never Says
poems.text:
Even after all this time
The sun never says to the earth,
'You owe me.'
Look what happens with a love like that.
It lights the whole sky.

poems.title: First Fig
Quiet Night Thought
poems.text:
Before my bed, the moon is shining bright,
I think that it is frost upon the ground.
I raise my head and look at the bright moon,
I lower my head and think of home.

poems.title: Ulysses
poems.text: Yes I said yes I will Yes.
